why_this_exists: Quiver Quantitative resells US federal contract awards; the source is USASpending.gov, free and keyless. Contract obligations are a demand signal that reaches the public before it reaches a 10-Q, and nothing in this project has used government spending data. It is a non-price, non-filing channel, which is the orthogonality argument the queue ranks highest.

data.source: api.usaspending.gov /api/v2/search/spending_by_category/recipient/, award types A-D (contracts), spending_level transactions, aggregated per calendar quarter by action date, top 1,000 recipients per quarter, 2012Q1 onward
data.parent_mapping: /api/v2/recipient/{id}/ parent_name for each recipient; amounts summed to parent
data.issuer_mapping: parent_name normalised (case, punctuation, legal suffixes) and matched EXACTLY to SEC FSDS filer names; no fuzzy matching, so a match is either right or absent. Match rate on dollars is reported.

point_in_time.publication_lag: DoD contract actions are published to FPDS with a 90-day delay. Every quarter's obligations are therefore treated as usable only from 91 days after the quarter ends, for all agencies, conservatively.
point_in_time.known_violation_declared: parent relationships are as of today, not as of the award. A subsidiary bought in 2020 is credited to its 2026 parent in 2015. This is lookahead in the mapping and biases toward finding something; a pass would need a robustness check excluding acquired subsidiaries.

signal.name: trailing-four-quarter obligation growth
signal.definition: log(TTM obligations ending at the latest usable quarter / TTM obligations ending four quarters earlier). Both TTM values must be at least $1M. Negative obligations (de-obligations) are included in the sums.
signal.declared_sign: POSITIVE: rising federal demand predicts higher subsequent returns. A negative result is a refutation, not a short signal.

measurement.decisions: quarterly, first trading week after 2013-04-01 through the last decision with a complete 13-week forward window
measurement.universe: issuers with a matched parent, a usable signal, and a price on the weekly panel at execution
measurement.density_check_first: report issuers per decision; if the median is below 100 the decile screen is declared unreadable and the result is inconclusive, not negative
measurement.target: 13-week forward return on clean_full_history_prices_v1, from the first weekly bar after the decision -- the same horizon and panel as Step 296
measurement.measures: rank IC, top-minus-bottom decile spread, decile monotonicity, block bootstrap p (block 4), placebo of 200 within-decision shuffles, leave-one-SIC2-out and leave-top-10-names-out
measurement.cumulative_search_note: one trial here, on top of every signal this project has screened on the same price panel

screen_pass_requires_all: mean IC > 0 in both halves of the decision sample
real mean IC above the placebo 95th percentile
if_it_passes: no book is built in this step. A pass earns a pre-registered book with the four Step 293 gates and the CLAUDE.md cost ladder, and the acquired-subsidiary robustness check, in a later step.
